21.heading: in:
refs: Dr. Lightfoot well observes, "that σοφια [ G4678 ], του [ G5120 ], Θεου [ G2316 ], the wisdom of God, is not to be understood of that wisdom which had God for its author, but of that wisdom which had God for its object. There was, among the heathen, σοφια [ G4678 ], της φυσεως, wisdom about natural things, that is philosophy

and σοφια [ G4678 ], του [ G5120 ], Θεου [ G2316 ], wisdom about God, that is, divinity. But the world, in its divinity, could not, by wisdom, know God." The wisest of the heathen had no just and correct views of the Divine nature
of which the works of Cicero and Lucretius are incontestable proofs.
